name: Doodle
tagline: Run group availability polls and convert the selected option into a calendar event

pricing.notes: Typical Pro monthly rate; annual billing can be lower.

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: 1 Booking Page, 1 one-to-one page, max 10 time slots/group poll, max 20 sessions/sign-up sheet and up to 1,000 participants/group poll
tiers.notes: Invitations must be shared manually; sending invitations from Doodle requires paid Professional.

tiers.name: Pro
tiers.limits: 1 user; unlimited group polls, one-to-ones, Booking Pages and sign-up sheets; up to 1,000 participants/group poll

tiers.name: Team
tiers.limits: 2–100 seats, unlimited scheduling per user and up to 5 hosts per Booking Page

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: More than 100 users, SSO/SAML, dedicated account management, advanced reporting and SLA

pricing.freeTierCaps: 1 Booking Page, 1 one-to-one page, 10 time slots/group poll, 20 sessions/sign-up sheet and up to 1,000 participants/group poll
pricing.hiddenCosts: Team has a 2-seat minimum. Annual subscribers can request a full refund within 14 days; monthly refunds are limited to rights required by law. Enterprise features and pricing require a quote.

verdictSummary: The core loop is buildable, but a dependable replacement becomes a real weekend or multi-day project. For Doodle, run group availability polls and convert the selected option into a calendar event. The hard boundary is participant familiarity, calendar connections, reminders, branding, and hosted delivery, plus calendar integrations and reliability.
coreLoopDIY: Run group availability polls against one calendar, convert the selected option into a conflict-safe calendar event, and send confirmations and reminders.
whatYouLose: participant familiarity, calendar connections, reminders, branding, and hosted delivery
ongoingBurden: OAuth refresh, webhooks, timezone databases, race conditions, reminders, deliverability, privacy, and uptime
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Doodle because people pay because one double booking or missed invite can cost more than years of subscription fees. The recurring cost buys OAuth refresh, webhooks, timezone databases, race conditions, reminders, deliverability, privacy, and uptime, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Cal.com
priorArt.desc: Mature open-source scheduling platform with calendar integrations and booking workflows.

alternatives.name: Calendly Free
alternatives.desc: One active event type and unlimited bookings; meeting polls survive, workflows and teams do not.

facts.install: Hosted signup and one calendar connection
facts.dataFormat: Event-type settings, invitee answers, scheduling activity and account data live in Calendly's cloud; confirmed meetings are synchronized to the connected calendar, and the internal storage format is not disclosed.
facts.gapVsPaid: Calendly's free poll can find a time, but its account- and event-type-oriented workflow is less frictionless for ad-hoc group voting than Doodle's dedicated poll flow.
facts.setupBlocker: Setup is clean, but the permanent free account is limited to one one-to-one event type and one connected calendar.

alternatives.name: Nextcloud Polls
alternatives.desc: Excellent Doodle replacement hiding inside a whole Nextcloud server; the poll is easy, the platform is not.

facts.install: Install or enable the Polls app inside an existing Nextcloud server
facts.dataFormat: Polls, options, votes, comments and invitations live in the operator's Nextcloud database; spreadsheet and HTML exports are available, and calendar-conflict hints use the user's Nextcloud calendar data.
facts.gapVsPaid: Nextcloud Polls is a strong poll engine, but installing an entire Nextcloud server and manually handling final calendar follow-through is far more work than sending a Doodle link.
facts.setupBlocker: The poll app is easy only after Nextcloud exists; the first obstacle is installing and maintaining an entire Nextcloud server for one small polling job.

alternatives.name: Rallly
alternatives.desc: Doodle’s useful half, date polls, votes, comments and finalization, without the account ambush.

facts.install: Use the hosted service with no install, or run the official single-server Docker Compose stack
facts.dataFormat: Rallly Cloud stores polls, votes, comments and account data in Rallly's infrastructure; self-hosting stores primary data in PostgreSQL and uploads in bundled Garage S3-compatible object storage or configured external Postgres/S3.
facts.gapVsPaid: Rallly closely matches date voting, but the hosted free service deletes expired inactive polls and the free self-hosted edition permits only one registered account.
facts.setupBlocker: Hosted free polls are deleted after every option is past and 30 inactive days; self-hosting is free for one registered user only, with multi-user administration requiring a perpetual license.

alternatives.name: TidyCal Free
alternatives.desc: Unlimited one-person booking types and paid bookings on one calendar; group meetings and fancy emails cost extra.

facts.install: Hosted signup and one calendar connection
facts.dataFormat: Booking types, attendee answers and booking records live in TidyCal's cloud and are synchronized to the connected calendar; the internal storage format is not disclosed.
facts.gapVsPaid: TidyCal Free is mainly a one-person booking-link product and does not provide Doodle's core anonymous group-availability poll workflow on the free plan.
facts.setupBlocker: There is no technical install hurdle, but free accounts get only one calendar connection and omit automatic video links, group meetings, custom emails, exports, analytics and API access.

alternatives.name: YouCanBookMe Free
alternatives.desc: One booking page, but it keeps forms, payments, confirmations, polls and the calendar-overlay trick.

facts.install: Hosted signup and one calendar connection
facts.dataFormat: Booking-page configuration, form answers and appointment records live in YouCanBookMe's cloud, with events synchronized to the connected calendar; the internal storage format is not disclosed.
facts.gapVsPaid: YouCanBookMe's single free booking page is more configurable but less immediate than Doodle for a one-off group poll, and additional pages or calendars require payment.
facts.setupBlocker: The setup itself is clean; the first hard limit is one booking page and one connected calendar.

alternatives.name: zcal Free
alternatives.desc: Polls, calendar overlay, voting deadlines and finalization are free; the ads are also absent.

facts.install: Hosted signup and calendar OAuth connection
facts.dataFormat: Scheduling links, availability, poll votes, answers and booking records live in zcal's cloud and synchronize to connected Google or Microsoft calendars; the internal storage format is not disclosed.
facts.gapVsPaid: zcal Free is a capable poll replacement, but Doodle still has the more established participant workflow, calendar integrations, organization controls, and large-group familiarity.
facts.setupBlocker: Calendar OAuth is straightforward; team routing, deeper branding and some business controls require a paid plan.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Pro plan and a single-user booking service DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for Doodle in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, Drizzle ORM, Google Calendar OAuth, and Resend; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: run group availability polls against one calendar, convert the selected option into a conflict-safe calendar event, and send confirmations and reminders.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Implement one account with configurable working hours, buffers, minimum notice, and booking horizon.
Connect Google Calendar using OAuth and store refresh tokens encrypted at rest.
Calculate availability in UTC and render it in the visitor's detected timezone.
Reserve slots transactionally, create calendar events, and prevent concurrent double booking.
Send confirmation, cancellation, and reminder email with signed management links.
Add an admin booking list, event-type editor, audit log, and calendar reconnect flow.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out Microsoft and Apple calendar support.
Deliberately leave out team round-robin routing.
Deliberately leave out payments, CRM workflows, and enterprise controls.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
